applied.evidence: All 25 titles are jellyfish cards (Jellyfish Diet/Stingers/Life Cycle/Sting Care...), but 'bantol' is not a jellyfish: Wolff's Dictionary of Cebuano Visayan has 'bantul n k.o. small, excellent eating fish with poisonous spines... and a frog-like face', and binisaya.com glosses bantol = stonefish (Synanceja verrucosa). Wolff's Cebuano jellyfish words are bukya, buruy (general name for jellyfish), bulbug, sabay, dangkalan. Corpus: bantol 0 bodies / 25 titles; dikya 42 Cebuano bodies (46 Tagalog bodies), and the bodies of these very cards say dikya (ffct-01826 'Ang dikya mokaon og gagmay nga mga mananap', ffct-03270, ffct-04714). A Cebuano-only child reads these 25 cards as being about a venomous bottom-dwelling fish.

'landok' is Ilocano for iron (Wiktionary lists Ilocano only; no Cebuano/Hiligaynon entry), it has NO entry in Wolff's Cebuano dictionary (0 occurrences of landuk/landok in the whole dictionary text) and none on binisaya.com. Corpus: landok 0 bodies / 12 titles; the concept words the bodies actually use are puthaw 440 bodies for iron (ffct-02360 title 'Kakulang sa Landok Anemya' -> body 'Kon kulang og puthaw ang lawas'), and bakal 42 / asero 22 for steel (ffct-24923 title 'Semento Piga Landok Hila' -> body 'gisagol... ang semento ug bakal'); Wolff: 'asiru n 1 steel'. Use puthaw on the iron cards (ffct-02360, ffct-20659, ffct-21586, ffct-23726, ffct-27998) and bakal/asero on the steel ones (ffct-20686, ffct-24923, ffct-25363, ffct-25944, ffct-26597, ffct-27285, plus ffct-27118 metals).

All 10 titles mean shivering/vibrating (Heat From Shivering, Chills Before Fever, Eardrum Vibrates With Sound), but 'kangi' is not a word: 0 standalone occurrences anywhere in Wolff's Cebuano dictionary (headwords or example sentences), no binisaya.com entry, no Wiktionary page in any language (404), 0 hits in the Bloom Cebuano books. The 99 'bodies' the prefix-matching tool reports are kangitngit (darkness). Corpus: kangi 0 bodies / 10 titles vs mokurog 58, pagkurog 35, kurog 8 bodies -- and the bodies of these exact cards say kurog (ffct-00120 'mangurog kung bugnaw kay ang pagkurog naghimo og init'; ffct-07483 'Ang pagkurog mao ang paspas nga paglihok sa atong kaunuran'). Wolff 'kurug' covers both senses, incl. machine vibration ('Ang kurug sa makina'), so pagkurog also serves ffct-09699 and ffct-16917.

buhag: 0 bodies as a word, 9 titles. The 5 substring hits are a different word entirely — mobuhagay/mibuhagay 'gush/flow out' (ffct-03953 'dugo nga mibuhagay', ffct-30925 'mobuhagay ang lava', ffct-39839 'hinay mobuhagay ang honey') — so the corpus has no 'buhag' meaning 'makes'. The titles use it for two unrelated concepts at once, which is itself proof it is unanchored: 8 cards mean 'makes/builds' and ffct-01293 means 'blowhole'. For 'makes/builds' the corpus word is himo — 8906 bodies — and it is what these very cards' bodies say: ffct-11389 'naghimo og protina', ffct-05809 'naghimo og bag-ong red blood cells', ffct-04928 'ang bakterya nga naghimo sa nata', ffct-08170 'naghimo og daghang bitamina', ffct-14426 'maghimo og init'; the agent noun is tighimo. For the blowhole card the corpus word is lungag (323 bodies; across the 6 blowhole cards lungag is the body rendering) and ffct-01293's own body says 'lungag sa ibabaw sa ulo'. So ffct-01293 needs lungag and the other 8 need naghimo/himo; all 9 are wrong as written.

liwang: 0 bodies as a word, 8 titles. The 2 substring hits are kaliwang = 'left (side)' (ffct-01321 'kaliwang baga', ffct-10019 'kaliwang ventricle') — a different word, and the wrong meaning for these cards. Every one of the 8 titles means light-in-weight, and every matching body writes gaan/magaan: ffct-05220 'Gaan kaayo ang lawas sa langgam', ffct-08443 'Ang balhibo sa langgam gaan apan lig-on', ffct-14967 'molutaw kung mas gaan kini', ffct-15485 'super magaan nga metal', ffct-16500 'mas gaan ang abo', ffct-00322 'Sobra kagaan ang ilang liso'. Corpus counts: gaan 546 bodies / 52 titles, magaan 60 bodies, vs liwang 0.

kagaangan: 0 bodies, 8 titles. The only gaan-family nouns the bodies actually use are kagaan / pinakagaan = 'lightness / lightest' (31 hits), so read as Cebuano the token says lightness, not reef. The corpus word for reef is bahura: 105 bodies / 28 titles, and it is the dominant Cebuano noun in reef cards (of 127 cards whose title_en contains 'reef', 70 bodies use bahura). Every example here proves it card-by-card — title says Reef, its own body says bahura: ffct-01127 'Ang bahura morag paril sa dagat', ffct-01180 'aron mahimo ang dagko nga bahura', ffct-03793 'naglibot ang reef shark sa bahura', ffct-08845 'manunukob sa bahura', ffct-11630 'Ang bahura sa korales', ffct-00444 'mobalhin sa bahura'.

kapeckan: 0 bodies, 0 English, 0 Tagalog, 8 titles — it is not a Cebuano word in this corpus in any form (no ka-pe... family member exists in the bodies; it looks like a mangled kapeligrohan). The corpus renders 'danger/dangerous' as peligro (281 bodies / 50 titles), delikado (326 bodies / 48 titles), katalagman (33 bodies / 23 titles) and kakuyaw (22 bodies), and those are exactly what these cards' own bodies say: ffct-02526 'pasidan-an ... kon adunay nagkaduol nga kakuyaw', ffct-15779 'Usa ka makahilo nga gas ... delikado kaayo', ffct-27838 'Delikado nga lamon ang gagmay nga magnetic beads', ffct-29260 'Ngano nga delikado ang PEIS Intensity VII'. Two of the eight are not even about danger — ffct-06876 is 'damage' (body: 'gidaot sa ilaga ang humay') and ffct-13041 is 'stored food saves lives' (body: 'kon wala nay makaon') — which confirms the token carries no stable meaning; all 8 titles are affected.

`--bis sugad` = 0 Cebuano bodies, 8 titles; absent from Wolff's Dictionary of Cebuano Visayan (accent/o-u-normalised search) and binisaya.com returns "No results found for the Cebuano word sugad" (nearest suggestions sugod/sukad/sugat). It is not the corpus's word for light: `--bis kahayag` = 1591 bodies / 442 titles, `--bis suga` = 341 bodies. Every one of the 8 cards' own bodies says kahayag, never sugad (ffct-23484 'ang kahayag mobiyahe sa tul-id nga linya'; ffct-23326 'ang itom mao ang kawalay kahayag'; ffct-23478 'Kon daghan ang gigikanan sa kahayag'), and the parallel TL titles all say Liwanag/Ilaw. Whatever 'sugad' is (it is the Waray/Bikol word for 'like, such as'), it does not deliver the 'Light' every title_en asserts.

`--bis yabo` = 1 body and that single body means pouring/emptying, not fog: ffct-08616 'Ang pag-yabo sa tubig gikan sa mga sudlanan' (EN: 'Emptying water from containers'). Wolff's yabu is likewise 'throw/pour water' ('pirmihag yabu sa hinúgas'). The corpus's fog word is gabon: `--bis gabon` = 41 bodies / 17 titles, and `--en \bfog` shows gabon 40 occurrences as the top content word of the 68 fog cards (hamog 9, panganod 14). Each of the 8 cards' own bodies says gabon (ffct-30355 'Ang gabon gilangkuban sa daghan kaayong gagmayng tinulo sa tubig'; ffct-34846 'makahimo kini og baga nga gabon sa Baguio'), except ffct-32630 which uses hamog; none uses yabo. TL titles say Hamog/Ambon.

applied.evidence: `--bis bukagnon` = 0 bodies, 7 titles; not in Wolff; binisaya.com resolves it only as root bukag 'basket' + affix -non, never as an insect. The corpus's bee word is putyokan/putyukan: `--bis putyukan` = 85 bodies, `--bis putyokan` = 50 bodies, `--en \bbee` ranks putyukan 101 / putyokan 72 / buyog 35 as the characteristic words of the 339 bee cards. All 7 cards' own bodies name the bee as putyokan/putyukan (ffct-01685 'mosayaw ang putyokan og espesyal nga sayaw'; ffct-13199 'Ang talo nga gigamit sa putyukan'), and the parallel TL titles all say Bubuyog. 'Bukagnon' does not deliver the 'Bee' of every title_en.

`--bis gatlang` = 0 bodies, 7 titles; absent from Wolff (o/u- and accent-normalised) and binisaya.com answers 'No results found for the Cebuano word gatlang' (it only offers the unrelated gutling). The corpus renders expansion gaps with gintang/puwang/luna: `--bis gintang` = 32 bodies / 4 titles, `--bis puwang` = 21 bodies, `--bis luna` = 139 bodies; `--en \bgap` ranks lungag 26, gintang 24, puwang 17, luna 17 across 129 gap cards. Every one of the 7 cards' own bodies uses one of those and never gatlang (ffct-15550 'may gagmayng gintang aron may luna sila molapad'; ffct-16795 'gagmayng puwang tunga-tunga sa mga riles'; ffct-15561 'may luna para sa paglapad'), and the TL titles all say Puwang. Note gintang is dictionary-attested ('May gintang dyis mitrus ang balay sa karsáda').

'gibiya-ong' 0 Cebuano bodies, 0 of 27,783 quiz-bank items, 0 in the CPT Cebuano corpora — unsourced. The corpus word for weight/mass is 'gibug-aton' (295 bodies, 20 bis titles, 487 quiz) with 'timbang' (103 bodies, 52 weight/mass titles) alongside; all six example bodies use gibug-aton or timbang. The only attested biya- root in the corpus is gibiyaan = left/abandoned, which is not weight.

'kuruy'/'kuroy' 0 hits in 47,056 Cebuano bodies, 0 in the 27,783-item quiz bank, 0 across the CPT Cebuano corpora — unsourced in any register. The corpus word for shiver/vibrate is 'kurog': 8 exact bodies, 34 'mokurog' hits inside cards whose English contains 'vibrat', 320 quiz hits, and other bis titles already use it (pagkurog 25, kurog 11). Each example card contradicts its own title — ffct-00451 body 'Mokurog ang lawas', ffct-23276 'nagkurog o naglihok dali balikbalik' — and their terms fields list kurog/pagkurog/nagkurog.

'dapit' in the corpus means place/spot or to adjoin — 576 body hits, all locational (ffct-00020 'Hugasi ang dapit', ffct-00082 'motubo sa laing dapit'), and quiz-04860 uses the exact form: 'nagdapit sa baybayon sa Pilipinas' = adjoins the coastline. It never means endangered. Endangered/threatened is 'nameligro' (47 bodies, 6 bis titles, 51 quiz) or 'namiligro' (34 bodies); all five example bodies use namiligro/nameligro while the titles say Endangered/Threatened.

'lagtaw' 0 hits in 47,056 bodies, 0 in the quiz bank, 0 in the raw and synthetic CPT Cebuano corpora — unsourced, and no near-spelling supports an 'adult' sense ('laktaw' = skip, 1 body, leap year). The corpus word is 'hamtong': 179 bodies, 163 hits inside cards whose English contains 'adult', 486 quiz, 8 bis titles; 'hingkod' (24 bodies) is the secondary. Every example body uses hamtong or hingkod, and the tl titles all say Matanda.

The corpus does use katkat — but for CLIMBING, never itching: 18 body hits (mokatkat 13, makakatkat 3, nagakatkat 1, pagkatkat 1) e.g. ffct-00520 'nagakatkat nga palma — mokatkat kini sa kahoy', and 42 quiz hits such as 'mokatkat sa makinis nga ibabaw' (climb smooth surfaces). Itch is 'katol' (18 bodies, 73 quiz), with kati (4 bodies) and pangatol. All five example bodies use katol/kati/pangatol against an itch title — ffct-02240 'kusog nga katol sa lubot', ffct-06845 'kati', ffct-12700 'pangatol'.

All five title_en are store/storage ("The Vacuole Storage Sac", "Fats Store Energy", "Bulbs Store Food Below", "Gabi's Starchy Corm", "Liver Stores Glycogen"), but `tipanan` is the appointment/rendezvous word (from tipan; Filipino/Bisaya glosses: appointment, rendezvous, date, tryst) — not storage. `tipanan` 0 bodies. The corpus's storage vocabulary: `tipiganan` 15 bodies (ffct-00902 "tipiganan sa pagkaon" = food storage; ffct-04467 "ang tipiganan kinahanglan dili sobra kabugnaw" = its storage), `tipigan` 48, `gitipigan` 121, `nagtipig` 137. The bodies of these very cards use the tipig root (ffct-03414 "Nagtipig kini og tubig", ffct-07857 "nagtipig og kusog", ffct-10973 "nagtipig og pagkaon", ffct-14008 "nagtipig og starch") while the titles head them with a word for a meeting — the kulob/lingkod shape.

applied.evidence: All five cards are forest/canopy cards, but `kagsuban` is not a Cebuano word: 0 of 47,056 bodies, no entry on binisaya.com (its fuzzy suggestions return kagub-anan, kasub-anan, kasubaan, kausaban — sorrow/river/change words, never forest), no web attestation, and it is not a well-formed derivation of gubat (kag- is not a Cebuano prefix; the letters do not reduce to kagubatan). The corpus word for forest is `lasang` 231 bodies / 44 titles and `kagubatan` 60 bodies / 23 titles — and the bodies of these five cards themselves say it: ffct-04015 "mananap sa lasang", ffct-07403 "nahibiling parte sa kagubatan", ffct-10077 "pagputol sa kagubatan", ffct-11141 "pagpanguha sa kalasangan", ffct-14604 "canopy sa lasang".

`dudon` 0 bodies. Wiktionary lists dudon only as ILOCANO (locust) and Bolinao (grasshopper) — Cebuano is not among its languages; the Cebuano cognate is `dulon`, and this corpus uses dulon exactly once, for locusts specifically (ffct-04006 "Ang kuliglig dili dulon"). Same class as the audit's `landok` finding (Ilocano for iron). The corpus's grasshopper vocabulary is `tipaklong` 11 bodies / 5 titles, `apan-apan` 7 bodies, plus bare `apan` and `balang` (ffct-03255 "Ang balang usa ka matang sa apan"). The bodies of the five cards themselves say apan or tipaklong for the animal the title calls dudon (ffct-04899/05088/10000 "Ang apan...", ffct-10731 "tingog sa tipaklong", ffct-13639 "dalunggan sa tipaklong").

All five title_en are about SPREADING (R0 disease spread, how germs spread, how fire spreads, heat spreads), but tapak is the step-on/patch word: 5 bodies, all literal (ffct-20827 "murag solid kung tapakan", ffct-26457 "mutapak ka sa tumoy sa diving board", ffct-30059 "unang tawo nga nakatapak sa Bulan"), and binisaya.com glosses tapak = patch / mend by putting a patch on. `pagkatapak` 0 bodies. The corpus renders spread as `pagkaylap` 31 / `mokaylap` 67 (kaylap* 192 bodies), `pagkatap` 21 (katap* 144), `pagkatag` 48 / mokatag (katag-forms 288). Smoking gun: ffct-07727's title says "R0 sa Pagkatapak sa Sakit" while its own body says "Unsa ang R0 sa pagkaylap sa sakit?"; likewise ffct-14514 body "mokaylap", ffct-15395 "mokalat", ffct-16843/22829 "mokatag".

Tagalog CV-reduplication grafted onto a Cebuano root. Corpus: paghahabol 0 bodies / 5 titles (0 in tl, en, terms); paghabol 7 bodies (ffct-03242 'sentro sa paghabol og pinya nga panapton', ffct-16161 'maayo kaayo ang uway sa paghabol'), habol 43 bodies / 12 titles used for weaving in titles already ('Habol sa Hyacinth | Hyacinth Weaving', 'Habol nga Pilipino | Filipino Weaving'). Wolff: 'habul 1 v [A; a] weave with a hand loom' — the Cebuano gerund is paghabol, never paghahabol. Decisive: two of these five cards' own bodies write the right word (ffct-17767 'Gitawag kini nga paghabol'; ffct-20479 'Ang paghabol ba sa piña fibers'), and every tl twin is 'Paghahabi ng X', so the bis title was built on the Tagalog gerund shape. As written it is the Tagalog word for chasing (Tag. habol = chase; Tag. weaving = paghahabi), not weaving.

Unattested string (0 bodies / 4 titles, 0 tl/en/terms) whose nearest real word is Tagalog kaugalian = custom/habit/tradition — wrong for dry scaly skin, survival traits, or a gene-coded eye colour. Wolff has no ugali/kaugalian entry at all (accent-stripped scan: 0 hits; the only ugal- words are kaugalingon 'one's own' 53 and ugaling 'however'). The Cebuano word for a trait is kinaiya: 312 bodies / 111 titles, and Wolff glosses it as character/nature ('Ang mainantusun nga kinaiya ni Husi'; 'Dunut nga kinaiya'). Three of these four cards' own bodies already say kinaiya (ffct-04030 'adunay kinaiya nga haom sa palibot', ffct-05935 and ffct-10233 'tagubilin/panudlo para sa usa ka kinaiya'), the tl twins all say Katangian, and the corpus title twin is decisive: ffct-06429 'Kinaiya sa Reptil | What Makes a Reptile' against ffct-02465 'Kaugalion sa Reptilya | What Makes a Reptile'.

panangka = 0 of 47,056 Cebuano bodies (0 en/tl/terms), 4 titles — the 4 example cards are the whole set. binisaya.com resolves it only as pa- + nangka = jackfruit (artocarpus heterophyllus); the nearest real words are sangka (battle/competition) and panangga (shield) — none is hunting. All 4 title_en are hunting cards and the corpus word is pangayam: pagpangayam 69 bodies, mangayam 54, mangangayam 30, bare pangayam 6. Decisive: every one of the 4 cards' OWN bodies says pagpangayam (ffct-02644 'nag-uban ang mga bayeng leon sa pagpangayam', ffct-02791/11678 'sobrang pagpangayam', ffct-14150 'iligal nga pagpangayam'), their tl twins say Pangangaso, and their terms carry pangayam / pagpangayam / nangayam.

pamahong = 0 bodies, and no pamaho* form appears in any of the 47,056 Cebuano bodies; 4 titles = all its cards. binisaya.com parses pamahong as pa- + pahong and glosses it 'dunce' (a stupid person) — it has no smell-faculty sense; the odour noun baho (304 bodies) is a different word and is not the faculty. All 4 title_en are sense-of-smell cards and the corpus renders that as panimaho (30 bodies), panimho (7), manimaho (4). Decisive: all four cards' own bodies use it — ffct-04488 'hilabihan ka talas nga panimaho', ffct-06751 'Maayo kaayo ang panimaho sa baboy', ffct-06781 'mas talinis manimaho', ffct-12797 'kusgan kaayo nga panimaho' — and all four terms lists literally contain 'panimaho' beside tl 'Pang-amoy'.

imoy = 0 Cebuano bodies (0 en/tl/terms), 4 titles = all its cards. binisaya.com has it only as imo + -y, the possessive pronoun 'your' — no smell sense at all, so 'Baboy Imoy Dili Mata' reads as 'pig your not eye'. All 4 title_en are smell-vs-sight cards and their own bodies carry the real word: ffct-07334 'nagsalig kini sa panimaho', ffct-11458 'maayo kaayo ang ilang panimaho', ffct-08203 'hait niyang panimho', ffct-11652 'pangsimhot ... simhoton una niini'. Corpus: panimaho 30 bodies, panimho 7, simhoton 5; tl twins all say Pang-amoy/Amoy and three of the four terms lists contain panimaho.

balit = 0 Cebuano bodies as a word, 4 titles = all its cards; binisaya.com returns 'No results found for the Cebuano word balit'. The only real neighbours in the corpus are balit-ad 12 bodies / balitad 5 = inverted/upside-down (ffct 'Balit-ad nga Hangin' = inversion layer) and balita 33 = news — neither is 'change'. All 4 title_en are change/transformation cards (Lens Shape Shifting, Pupa Transformation, Caramel Chemical Change, inertia = resisting change of motion) and the corpus word is kausaban 214 bodies / pagbag-o 289 / nag-usab 235. Decisive: the cards' own bodies say 'Nag-usab og porma ang lente', 'halos hingpit nga giusab ang lawas', 'usa ka kemikal nga pagbag-o', 'mosukol sa bisan unsang kausaban sa iyang lihok'; tl twins are Nagbabago/Pagbabago and the terms fields carry 'nag-usab og porma', 'nagbag-o', 'paglikay sa kausaban'.

Bare batan = 0 Cebuano bodies, 4 titles = all its cards; it is the hyphenated adjective with its suffix cut off, not a word on its own (binisaya.com has no standalone batan; its parser resolves the string to balat + -an, sea cucumber). The real form is heavily attested and already on the cards: batan-on 130 bodies, batan-ong 103, plus 8 bis titles ('Batan-ong Pako', 'Batan-ong Tanom'). Decisive: the bodies of these very cards say 'batan-ong lapu-lapu' (ffct-09152), 'Paspas modako ang batan-ong ilaga' (ffct-11899), 'Ang mga bata pa nga bukid' (ffct-30024), 'linghod pa' (ffct-08029), and the terms fields of ffct-09152 and ffct-11899 literally list 'batan-on'. tl twins: Batang Lapu-Lapu, Batang Daga, Bata at Matatandang Bundok.

tag-uha: 0 Cebuano bodies, 0 tl/en, 4 titles only. The corpus word for drought is hulaw (51 bis bodies, 4 bis titles; huwaw 5 more). All 4 cards mean drought and their own material says so: ffct-31612's body literally defines it — 'Ang hulaw (drought) dugay nga panahon nga halos walay ulan' — while its bis title says 'Drought sa Tag-uha' (drought-in-the-drought); its terms field carries 'huwaw','hulaw' and never tag-uha. tl side uses the real Tagalog word tagtuyot (74 tl bodies), so tag-uha looks like an invented Cebuano parallel to it, not a word the body vocabulary knows.

katawo: 0 Cebuano bodies, 4 titles. Every example means BIRTH (title_en: Birth of an Iceberg, Star Birth in Nebulae, Born with Camouflage, born-river homing for salmon). The corpus renders birth as pagkatawo (14 bis bodies AND 7 bis titles) and natawo (72 bis bodies) — ffct-29074's tl title is 'Kapanganakan ng Iceberg' and ffct-12741's body says 'natawo na ang hayop'. Bare katawo is not the corpus's nominalisation; with the pag- stripped it reads off tawo/katawhan (person/people), so 'Katawo sa Nebula' does not deliver 'Star Birth'. Fix is the corpus's own title form: 'Pagkatawo sa Iceberg'.

asok: 0 Cebuano bodies, 0 Tagalog, 0 English, 4 titles. Cebuano smoke is aso — 195 bis bodies, 57 bis titles — and all four cards' OWN bodies use it ('mogamit og hinay nga aso', 'Ang init nga aso mosaka', 'mogawas og makahilo nga aso', 'humot sa kamanyang o aso'). The tl titles of the same cards say usok (173 tl bodies), so asok reads as a usok/aso blend rather than a Cebuano vowel variant (the attested variant pattern is vowel-level: itum/itom, daku/dako — not an added final -k). ffct-16203's terms list 'usok','aso' and never asok.

`daug` means win/defeat, not trail. Wolff's entry: daug = 'overcome', 'prevail', 'vanquish', and as a noun the winnings ("bahina ang daug" = divide the winnings); binisaya.com gives win / overthrow / prevail / vanquish and no spatial sense. Exact-word count in the pool: `daug` = 0 bodies / 3 titles (the 17 prefix hits are `daugdaugon` = oppress, ffct-08017 "dili daugdaugon"). The corpus word for the concept is right inside these very cards' bodies: ffct-00295 "Ang kuhol magbilin ug sinaw nga AGI sa uhog" under title "Daug nga Lika sa Kuhol" / Snail Slime Trail; ffct-08253 "magbilin kini og tag-as nga AGI sa damuhan" under "Daug sa Dugong" / Dugong Feeding Trails; ffct-09038 "Ang mga TUNOB sa tiil nagpakita" under "Daug sa Kawan sa Dinosaur" / Herd Footprint Fossils. Corpus counts: `agi` = 49 bodies, `agianan` = 308 bodies / 80 titles, `tunob` = 18 bodies (Wolff: tunub = footstep, imprint). All three Tagalog sides use 'bakas'. Use `agi` for the two trail cards; `tunob` is the closer fit for ffct-09038's footprint fossils.

lihog: 0 Cebuano bodies. Word-boundary grep over 47k bodies, the quiz bank and 11MB of Cebuano CPT text finds the root ONLY inside 'palihog' (= please / ask a favour; binisaya.com has palihog and lihogan, no plant sense). The corpus word for stem/stalk is punoan (189 bodies) / tangkay (104), and each of these three cards' OWN body uses punoan: ffct-01646 'tubig sa punoan', ffct-12822 'Ang punoan sa kangkong hungkag sa sulod', ffct-37862 'kabag-on sa pangunang punoan'. So 'Lihog sa Kangkong' reads as 'Kangkong's favour', not 'Kangkong Stems'.

matarong: 0 Cebuano bodies. binisaya.com gives only 'righteous / upright' — no sharpness sense — and the project's own Cebuano quiz text uses it adverbially for 'properly' ('dili nila matarong og hilis ang pagkaon' = 'can't properly digest'; 'atop nga wala matarong og taod' = 'roof not properly installed'). The corpus word for sharp is hait (236 bodies), and all three cards' own bodies use it: ffct-02597 'hait nga ngipon', ffct-13345 'pinaka-hait', ffct-32728 'Grabe ka hait kini'. Titles therefore say 'Righteous Teeth / Righteous Obsidian' where title_en says 'Sharp'.

gupos: 0 Cebuano bodies, 0 in the 27k-item quiz bank, 0 in 11MB of Cebuano CPT text, no entry in binisaya.com (it suggests gapos 'bind' / gupok 'crumble') and no Cebuano Wiktionary entry — unsourced everywhere except these 3 titles.
